paragraphs: Many fake bomb threats are causing problems in Europe this week. Some were sent to Irish radio and news companies.
On Thursday, an Aer Lingus plane flew from Dublin to Rome. Someone said there was a bomb on the plane. Two French fighter jets flew next to it. The plane landed at an air base in France.
All the passengers got off the plane. Police checked the bags. They found no bomb.
French police asked the two pilots some questions. Now the pilots can leave France. Aer Lingus says the crew did a very good job.
Nearly 30 flights had problems on Thursday. Italian schools also got 279 fake emails. Some experts think Russia may be behind the threats. Others say it is very hard to find the senders.
Next week, more than 50 European leaders will meet in Dublin. The Foreign Minister says the threats are very worrying.

有人說飛機上有炸彈。

飛機降落在法國的一個空軍基地。
所有乘客都下了飛機。

現在兩名機師可以離開法國了。
愛爾蘭航空說機組人員表現得非常好。

義大利的學校也收到279封假電子郵件。

paragraphs: A wave of false bomb threats has caused problems across Europe this week. Planes have changed course, schools in Italy have been emptied, and Irish media companies have also received threats.

On Thursday, Aer Lingus flight EI402 left Dublin for Rome. A message sent to Italian airports said there were explosives on board. Two French fighter jets went up and guided the plane to a military airbase at Évreux in France. The passengers left the plane and their bags were searched, but nothing dangerous was found.

French investigators then questioned the Irish pilot and the British co-pilot. They had been told that the pilot first refused to land. Both men were later allowed to leave France, but the investigation is still going on. Aer Lingus said its captain and crew behaved in a completely professional way.
Almost 30 flights in Europe were affected by fake threats on Thursday, and more came on Friday. In Italy, 279 false emails were sent to schools. No bombs were found anywhere and nobody was hurt.

The threat about the Dublin flight used the name of a small Russian group. However, an expert at the University of Salford, Anna Kruglova, does not believe the group sent it. She says emails like these are very hard to trace, and the senders want to frighten people and create chaos.

Some security experts think Russia could be behind the campaign, as part of attacks on countries that support Ukraine. Foreign Affairs Minister Helen McEntee called the events extremely worrying. More than 50 European leaders will meet in Dublin next week.

一則寄給義大利機場的訊息說機上有爆裂物。

法國調查人員隨後訊問了愛爾蘭籍機長和英國籍副機長。
他們接獲消息說機長起初拒絕降落。

paragraphs: A week-long wave of hoax bomb threats has disrupted travel and daily life across Europe, diverting flights, forcing the evacuation of Italian schools and targeting several Irish media organisations.

The most dramatic incident involved Aer Lingus flight EI402 from Dublin to Rome on Thursday. After a warning sent to Italian airports claimed that explosives were on board, two French fighter jets escorted the aircraft to the Évreux military airbase in northern France. Passengers were taken off and their luggage was searched, but no explosives were discovered.

French prosecutors questioned the Irish captain and his British co-pilot after receiving reports that the pilot had initially refused to land. The pair have since been permitted to leave France, although the prosecutor in Évreux said inquiries were continuing. Aer Lingus insisted that its crew had acted impeccably throughout.

Nearly 30 flights were disrupted by false threats on Thursday, with further incidents reported on Friday. Meanwhile, 279 fake bomb warnings were emailed to schools in Italy. No suspicious items have been found and nobody has been injured.

The message about the Dublin flight was signed in the name of a Russian extremist group. Anna Kruglova, a terrorism researcher at the University of Salford, considers it unlikely that the group was responsible. In her view, untraceable emails allow senders to borrow a frightening name in order to intimidate the public.

Several security analysts suspect the campaign is part of Russian 'hybrid warfare' aimed at destabilising countries that support Ukraine. Minister for Foreign Affairs Helen McEntee described the events as extremely concerning, particularly as more than 50 European leaders are due in Dublin next week.

最戲劇性的事件發生在週四從都柏林飛往羅馬的愛爾蘭航空EI402班機上。
一則寄給義大利機場的警告聲稱機上有爆裂物，隨後兩架法國戰鬥機將這架飛機護送到法國北部的埃夫勒軍用機場。
乘客被帶下飛機，行李遭到搜查，但沒有發現爆裂物。
法國檢察官接獲報告稱機長起初拒絕降落後，訊問了這名愛爾蘭籍機長及其英國籍副機長。
兩人之後已獲准離開法國，但埃夫勒的檢察官表示調查仍在持續。
愛爾蘭航空堅稱其機組人員自始至終表現無可挑剔。
週四有將近30個航班因假威脅受到干擾，週五又有更多事件傳出。
與此同時，有279封假炸彈警告以電子郵件寄到義大利的學校。
目前沒有發現可疑物品，也沒有人受傷。
有關都柏林航班的訊息是以一個俄羅斯極端主義團體的名義署名。
索爾福德大學的恐怖主義研究員安娜·克魯格洛娃認為該團體不太可能是幕後主使。
她認為，無法追蹤的電子郵件讓寄件者可以借用嚇人的名號來恐嚇大眾。
數名安全分析人士懷疑，這場行動是俄羅斯「混合戰」的一部分，目的在破壞支持烏克蘭國家的穩定。
外交部長海倫·麥肯蒂形容這些事件極度令人擔憂，尤其下週將有50多位歐洲領袖來到都柏林。

paragraphs: A week-long spate of hoax bomb threats has wreaked havoc across Europe, prompting flight diversions, the evacuation of Italian schools and a series of menacing messages aimed at Irish media outlets.

The most striking episode unfolded on Thursday, when Aer Lingus flight EI402, bound for Rome from Dublin, became the subject of a warning to Italian airports alleging that explosives had been stowed on board. Two French fighter jets were scrambled to escort the aircraft to the Évreux military airbase, where passengers disembarked and baggage was meticulously searched. Nothing untoward was found.

French prosecutors subsequently interviewed the Irish captain and his British co-pilot amid claims that the pilot had at first declined to land. Both men have since been cleared to leave French territory, though the inquiry remains ongoing. Aer Lingus has staunchly defended its crew, maintaining that they conducted themselves impeccably.

Close to 30 flights were thrown into disarray on Thursday alone, and fresh threats surfaced on Friday. In Italy, 279 bogus warnings were emailed to schools. Mercifully, no explosive devices have been detected and no injuries reported.

The message concerning the Dublin flight purported to come from an obscure Russian extremist group. Anna Kruglova, a terrorism scholar at the University of Salford, regards this attribution as implausible, arguing that anonymous emails are notoriously difficult to trace and that perpetrators often hijack sinister names simply to sow panic.

A number of security analysts discern the hallmarks of Russian 'hybrid warfare', designed to destabilise states that back Ukraine. Minister for Foreign Affairs Helen McEntee termed the developments extremely concerning, not least because over 50 European leaders are poised to converge on Dublin next week.
